item.title: ‘Made in Europe’ laws could derail UK plans for reset with EU
item.description: Government sources say legislation aimed at China poses a risk to British businesses and must be addressed European legislation that threatens to lock British business out of EU industry could derail a planned reset summit between the bloc and the UK, government sources have said. The “Made in Europe” legislation – formally known as the Industrial Accelerator Act – is designed to curb China’s increasing presence in European industry, but was not on the reset plan agreed by the former prime minister, Keir Starmer , and the European Commission chief, Ursula von der Leyen, in London in May 2025… Fuente: The Guardian - World.

item.title: Greens just four points behind Labour in urban areas, poll reveals
item.description: Exclusive: UK’s Green parties could take 40 seats if result replicated at next election, according to Labour-linked thinktank The Greens are just four points behind Labour in urban constituencies across the UK, putting them within touching distance of taking as many as 40 seats if the result was replicated at the next election, according to new polling by a Labour-linked thinktank. The survey by ThinkLabour, which has extensive links to Andy Burnham’s government, finds that urban voters have moved in large numbers towards the UK’s Green parties since the 2024 general election. The research… Fuente: The Guardian - World.

item.title: Syria's parliament votes to scrap Assad-era terrorism court, nullify rulings
item.description: Syria's parliament voted to abolish a counter-terrorism court established in 2012. This court was reportedly used to prosecute thousands of anti-Assad Syrians on terrorism charges. The decision formalizes the court's abolition after new authorities treated it as defunct. The United Nations Human Rights Committee had raised concerns over judicial guarantees and fair trials. This vote occurred after opposition forces removed Bashar al-Assad from power in December 2024. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.description: Seis meses después de su fallido intento de convertirse en la alcaldesa de París, Rachida Dati se enfrenta desde este miércoles a un juicio del que depende su reputación. Ha empezado en el Tribunal de París el proceso judicial a la exministra de Cultura francesa y a Carlos Ghosn, que fue el CEO de Renault entre 2005 y 2019. Los magistrados de instrucción sospechan que la dirigente conservadora cobró 900.000 euros de una filial del grupo automovilístico entre 2009 y 2012 , a cambio de utilizar su escaño en el Parlamento Europeo para defender los intereses de la multinacional.Desde el inicio de… Fuente: ABC España - Internacional.

item.title: Former French culture minister goes on trial over corruption charges
item.description: Rachida Dati accused of lobbying for carmaker Renault-Nissan when she was member of European parliament Rachida Dati , a former French culture minister, has gone on trial in Paris on corruption charges linked to dealings with the Renault-Nissan carmaking group. Dati, 60, is accused of illegal lobbying when she accepted €900,000 (£770,000) in lawyer’s fees from a Netherlands-based subsidiary of Renault-Nissan while she was a member of the European parliament. The court will have to decide what the money was for. Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - World.

item.title: Singapore ministers earn millions. What do other Asian leaders make?
item.description: Singapore’s ministers are among the world’s highest paid, a system its leaders have defended as necessary to attract capable people into public service and reduce the temptation of corruption. Its latest salary review has once again put the spotlight on that approach, while highlighting a wider regional divide over how Asian governments value political leadership and public service.
